title: A quantitative understanding of quark and gluon confinement and the QCD mass gap

concept.text: Strings 2000 problem 10 (proposed by Igor Klebanov and Oyvind Tafjord): can we quantitatively understand quark and gluon confinement in Quantum Chromodynamics and the existence of a mass gap? Sources given: https://preskill.caltech.edu/millennium.html ; https://aip.brightspotcdn.com/PTO.v54.i10.14_2.online.pdf ; https://x.com/martinmbauer/status/1779906631003697211.

change_log.change: Added by hand to PHY on 2026-11-15.
change_log.reason: One of the ten Physics Problems for the Next Millennium chosen at the Strings 2000 conference (University of Michigan) by a panel of Michael Duff, David Gross and Edward Witten; added at the owner's request, November 14, 2026.

page.title: Quark confinement and the QCD mass gap
page.definition: A derivation from four-dimensional quantum chromodynamics (QCD), the theory of quarks and gluons, of color confinement—only color-neutral particles occur in isolation—and a positive mass gap, the minimum excitation energy above the vacuum. The target is zero-temperature QCD with physical nonzero quark masses and without electromagnetic or weak interactions.

goal.need: Quark motion and gluon interactions account for approximately 99% of the proton’s mass. Lattice calculations already reproduce the masses of many hadrons. What those masses alone cannot explain is why an isolated quark or gluon never appears. A derivation of confinement would account for that observation, and a mass gap would explain why the nuclear force between protons and neutrons has a short range. Individual hadron masses would still require separate calculations and a measured input to set the mass scale.

statements.body: Strings 2000 selection panel: Michael Duff, David Gross and Edward Witten
statements.quote: Can we quantitatively understand quark and gluon confinement in Quantum Chromodynamics and the existence of a mass gap?
statements.context: Selected as problem 10, proposed by Igor Klebanov and Oyvind Tafjord, and presented on 15 July 2000.

statements.quote: Can QCD account quantitatively for the confinement of quarks and gluons inside hadrons?
statements.context: The report lists this as one of three basic questions about the structure of nuclear matter. It addresses the confinement part of the joint goal.

completion.title: Continuum QCD yields color confinement and a derived positive mass gap.
completion.criterion: A peer-reviewed construction of interacting continuum QCD in 3+1 dimensions, at zero temperature and density with physical nonzero quark masses, derives only SU(3)-singlet asymptotic particle states and a finite positive mass gap above the vacuum. It supplies a positive lower bound on the gap in terms of QCD parameters, with the infinite-volume and continuum limits controlled. Electromagnetic and weak interactions are excluded.
completion.set_by: Atlas; no external joint quantitative acceptance test was found for the full Strings 2000 QCD question.
completion.basis: Strings 2000, Clay’s official problem and prize rules, and the National Research Council’s 2013 report were searched; none specifies a joint quantitative acceptance test for this QCD question. Clay’s prize concerns pure Yang–Mills theory and does not require confinement. This test combines the published QCD properties without adding a numerical accuracy target.

milestones.title: A lattice gauge theory confines quarks in its strong-coupling limit.
milestones.criterion: At fixed lattice spacing, demonstrate confinement of external quarks in the strong-coupling limit of a gauge-invariant lattice gauge theory.
milestones.set_by: Wilson’s confinement criterion and strong-coupling construction, adopted in lattice gauge theory; Confinement of quarks (1974).
milestones.threshold_quote: The lattice gauge theory has a computable strong-coupling limit; in this limit the binding mechanism applies and there are no free quarks.

milestones.title: Lattice QCD reproduces the light-hadron spectrum after continuum extrapolation.
milestones.criterion: Calculate light meson and baryon masses with dynamical up, down and strange quarks. Tune the quark masses to the physical point, control finite-volume effects, and extrapolate to zero lattice spacing using at least three lattice spacings. For masses independent of the inputs used to tune the quark masses and set the scale, show agreement with experiment within the stated statistical and systematic uncertainties.
milestones.set_by: Dürr et al., criteria for a controlled light-hadron spectrum calculation, items I–V.
milestones.threshold_quote: no less than three values of the lattice spacing

milestones.title: Interacting continuum QCD satisfies the Wightman axioms in four spacetime dimensions.
milestones.criterion: Construct interacting continuum QCD in four spacetime dimensions with physical quark masses. Show that its physical correlation functions satisfy the Wightman axioms, including relativistic covariance, locality and positivity, and reproduce QCD at short distances.
milestones.set_by: Constructive quantum-field-theory existence criterion: Osterwalder and Schrader (1975), §IV.1. Jaffe–Witten §5 identifies existence of theories with additional matter fields as a separate target.

milestones.title: Continuum QCD has a finite positive mass gap above its vacuum.
milestones.criterion: For infinite-volume continuum QCD with physical nonzero quark masses, set the vacuum energy to zero. Prove that the infimum of the positive spectrum of the Hamiltonian is finite and strictly positive.
milestones.set_by: Jaffe and Witten, Quantum Yang–Mills Theory, §1, property 1 for QCD; this is distinct from their pure-Yang–Mills prize formulation.
milestones.threshold_quote:
there must be some constant ∆ > 0
such that every excitation of the vacuum has energy at least ∆.

milestones.title: Every asymptotic particle state of continuum QCD is a color singlet.
milestones.criterion: Derive from four-dimensional, infinite-volume continuum QCD with physical nonzero quark masses that every asymptotic particle state is invariant under the SU(3) color group. The derivation must exclude isolated states carrying color, including quarks and gluons.
milestones.set_by: Jaffe and Witten, Quantum Yang–Mills Theory, §1, property 2 for QCD.
milestones.threshold_quote:
the physical particle states—such as the proton,
neutron, and pion—are SU(3)-invariant.

not_found: No published programme prescribing an ordered sequence of intermediate tests for the full QCD question was found.
No academy or nuclear-physics roadmap statement was found disputing the value or feasibility of deriving confinement and a mass gap in physical QCD.

results.finding: In one exactly gauge-invariant lattice formulation, zero free quarks occur in the strong-coupling limit.
results.detail: The abstract reports that Lorentz and Euclidean invariance are absent in this limit.
results.quote: in this limit the binding mechanism applies and there are no free quarks.

results.finding: Across 14 lattice simulation points, the Ξ∗ mass in the Ω-scale analysis lies 1.32 combined standard errors above experiment.
results.detail: Table 1 gives 1.561 GeV for Ξ∗ in the Ω set versus 1.533 GeV experimentally. The 28 MeV difference exceeds the 21.2 MeV statistical and systematic uncertainty combined in quadrature.
results.quote:
With both scale-setting
procedures we ﬁnd that the masses agree with the hadron spectrum observed in nature (27).

results.finding: Light-hadron spectroscopy at six lattice spacings yielded a continuum nucleon mass of 941.7 MeV.
results.detail: The verdict uses the stable spectrum. The authors identify a finite-volume scattering analysis as necessary for a refined determination of the Δ, Σ* and Ξ* resonances.
results.quote:
we ﬁnd the nucleon massmN = 941 .7(6.5)(7.6) MeV and the other
stable baryon masses to agree with their experimental values

results.finding: The committee reports a continuum-limit proof for quantum Yang–Mills theory with fermion coupling in a 1,147-page proof package.
results.detail: The committee plans to check the Lean statement and its correspondence to the informal proof before release. The page count describes the proof package. The result has no sample size.
results.quote:
We were delighted to learn of the recent proof by OpenAI of the existence
of quantum Yang-Mills theory, including coupling to fermions.

results.finding: Lean verification of one pure Yang–Mills construction establishes Wightman axioms in 4 spacetime dimensions.
results.detail: The validation group checked the formal construction in Lean. Uniqueness of the infinite-volume limit and full perturbative agreement remain open.
results.quote:
In our judgment the submission proves that a relativistic
quantum field theory satisfying the Wightman axioms can be constructed as a scaling limit of
four-dimensional Wilson lattice gauge theory for any simple compact gauge group.

results.finding: Pure lattice Yang–Mills has a Wilson-loop area law down to β → 0 in the strong-coupling regime. The theorem uses no empirical sample.
results.detail: The proof applies to rectangular loops and gives a positive area-decay rate at each coupling in the stated regime, with constants independent of lattice volume.
results.quote:
In this note, we prove Wilson’s area law in the ’t Hooft regime of parameters, which improves
on a classical result of Osterwalder-Seiler from 1978, as well as on more recent work by the authors.

results.finding: PACS10’s three independent octet baryon masses, extrapolated from 60 gauge configurations, agree with pseudoexperimental values within 2σ in both conventions.
results.detail: The 60 configurations are from the three large-volume ensembles used in the continuum fits. A separate 800-configuration ensemble at the coarsest spacing supported the finite-volume check and mass reweighting.
results.quote:
In both conventions the octet baryon masses agree with the pseudoexperimental values within 2
σ
\sigma
error bands.

results.finding: Nine lattice ensembles give a continuum ρ Breit–Wigner mass of 781.6 ± 10.0 MeV at the physical pion mass.
results.detail: The main extrapolation omits strange-quark mass dependence. A refit with a kaon-mass term could not resolve that dependence. The uncertainty estimate includes differences among lattice irreducible representations.

results.finding: Eight lattice ensembles yield a continuum K*(892) pole mass of 882.10 MeV at physical pion and kaon masses.
results.detail: The abstract, Eq. 50, and Table 6 give 882.10 MeV. The conclusions give a different central value of 881.0 MeV.

goal.need = "Quark motion and gluon interactions account for approximately 99% of the proton\u2019s mass. Lattice calculations already reproduce the masses of many hadrons. What those masses alone cannot explain is why an isolated quark or gluon never appears. A derivation of confinement would account for that observation, and a mass gap would explain why the nuclear force between protons and neutrons has a short range. Individual hadron masses would still require separate calculations and a measured input to set the mass scale.". Reason: The current rationale omits the short range of the nuclear force and leaves unclear what a derivation would add to existing mass calculations.

add statement by National Research Council, 1999: "Can QCD account quantitatively for the confinement of quarks and gluons inside hadrons?". Reason: The Council’s 1999 report asks directly whether QCD explains confinement and identifies the particles to which the question applies.
